BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN HOOK (recorded because it is the exact failure RI-AUD01 names): hooking `emit` and classifying the event AT emit time sees `{f, kind}` only — every resolve.js call site fills the fields AFTER emit returns. The first probe run voiced 50 impacts across 7 materials and 4 weight tiers as `{hit_flesh_light:50, whiff:5}` — literally the one-sword.wav failure. Fixed by draining `_audioPending` at the END of CombatSystem.step(frame), same frame, events fully filled.
BUG 2: the player body's id is `P`, not `player`. C10 player_hurt is selected by `e.dst === playerId`, so the wrong id voices every blow the player TAKES as one they LAND.

REAL DEFECT FOUND IN THE SHIPPED BUILD, NOT FIXED (moving it would move trace bytes other pieces hold determinism baselines against): game/src/combat/system.js LEGACY_ALIAS.CRIT_HIT is `(e) => (e.kind === 'riposte' ? 'riposte' : 'backstab')` and is evaluated INSIDE the emit closure, one line after bus.emit() — before PlayerController._critDamage has written e.kind. sim/events.js:245 has just deleted every field but f and type, so e.kind is undefined and the ternary takes the else branch EVERY TIME. **Every riposte in the game is mirrored into the lower_snake trace stream as `backstab`.** RI-AUD01 §A makes C07 riposte and C08 backstab two separate mandatory classes. My driver reads e.kind at FLUSH time (end of step, after _critDamage wrote it) and classifies both correctly, which is how the disagreement surfaced.

INSTRUMENT DEFECT in tools/lib/combat-node.mjs: its bus stores the event TYPE in a field called `kind` ({f, kind}), while the engine's real bus (sim/events.js#emit) stores it in `type` and leaves `kind` free. PlayerController._critDamage writes `e.kind = m.id`, which is correct against the engine and CLOBBERS THE TYPE against the node arena — every CRIT_HIT vanishes from a node trace. Any node-arena tool counting CRIT_HIT sees zero, forever. My probe captures the type out-of-band; combat-node.mjs itself is untouched.

V9 BUG IN MY OWN DRIVER, FIXED: the same-frame same-class collapse map was keyed `frame|class` over the whole run. That is an unbounded leak AND a wrong answer when one driver sees many fixtures whose frame numbers restart — 17 voices silently collapsed. The map now holds one frame at a time.

MASS DEFECT MECHANISM (per-frame dump of whp_hist_bindings/r2, the worst clip, total=155 startup=63 active=11 recovery=81, arc_decl=305): the ENTIRE 305 degree arc is swept inside the 11 ACTIVE frames (f64-f74), ~28 deg/frame = 1660 deg/s, against a weapon whose hilt-to-tip length is 3.114 m -- so tip speed 163.3 m/s is omega*r, not a teleport and not a rounding error. The other two phases are worse than the peak: the 63-frame startup does a slow WANDERING ORBIT (2-24 m/s, tip circling the body) that is not anticipation, and the 81-frame recovery is COMPLETELY DEAD -- tip frozen at exactly (1.03,0.72,-3.11), speed 0.000 for 80 consecutive frames. RI-WPN05 §E follow-through requires >=0.20 of recovery frames still travelling; this clip achieves ~0.012. So ONE cause -- the arc lives only in the active window -- fails THREE §E rows at once (peak tip speed, follow-through fraction, tip speed continuity).

MASS: the lever arm is the multiplier and it is data, not code. WHP declares a 3.114 m hilt-to-tip socket span while sitting in the `medium` tier whose §E ceiling is 26 m/s. No angular profile that sweeps a declared 305 deg in 11 frames can hold 26 m/s at r=3.114 (it would need omega <= 8.35 rad/s = 478 deg/s = 7.97 deg/frame, i.e. 38 active frames). Either the arc, the active window, or the tier is wrong for whips; the peak-speed row cannot be solved by easing alone.

CALIBRATION GAP FOUND (this is the M3 hole): every one of the 48 variants ships norm_db = 0, and the live gain is 10^((peak_dbfs + norm_db)/20) applied to a SYNTH voice of arbitrary raw amplitude. hit_flesh_light declares -8 dBFS and actually renders at -2.143 + -8 = -10.14 dBFS. The declared 17.0 dB loudness ladder (parried -3 ... whiff -20) is therefore a CLAIM NOTHING HAS MEASURED: the true spread is whatever the 12 synth recipes happen to peak at. norm_db = -(raw peak dBFS) makes rendered == declared. Fix in progress.

M3 MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME AND IT FAILS (browser, OfflineAudioContext, 48 real renders): the RI-AUD01 §C ladder holds on only 9 of 11 rows, worst error 8.27 dB. Cause: the 12 synth recipes' RAW peaks spread 16.20 dB (parried +3.28 dBFS down to whiff -12.91 dBFS) and every norm_db was 0, so the shipped level is raw+declared and the declared ladder was never what came out.

M6 DEFECT FOUND, AND ONLY A MOVING TARGET COULD HAVE FOUND IT (browser, enemy orbiting the player at r=1.4 m through +/-40 deg while the player swings): every impact the PLAYER lands is logged with `src:'P'`, `distance_m: 0.000`, and a pan that never changes as the enemy moves -- pan held at -0.2728 while the target swung through theta -24, +18, -14.5, +16 deg. The pan tracks the PLAYER'S OWN YAW instead (pyaw 0 -> pan 0; pyaw 15.83 -> pan -0.2728 forever). Cause: game/src/audio/impact-audio.js line ~304 resolves the voice's world position as `posOf(e.src || e.who || e.dst)` -- the ATTACKER -- so a hit you land is positioned at your own feet and 'panned' by the negative of your own facing. Turn your head and the sword-on-flesh sound swings across the stereo field; move the enemy and it does not move at all. A STILL TARGET DEAD AHEAD WITH pyaw=0 GIVES pan=0, dist=0, WHICH LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A CORRECT CENTRED IMPACT -- this is the AGENT-PROTOCOL 'still target hides every steering defect' case, reproduced.

INSTRUMENT TRAP worth a successor's time: the browser combat trace is COLUMNAR (`{t:'F', f, i, p, e, x}` frame records), not an event list. Filtering it for a row whose `type` is 'hit' matches NOTHING and yields joined:0 -- a check that reports neither pass nor fail and looks like a quiet success. The geometry's own witness of a landed blow is a drop in `rec.e[i][3]` (enemy hp; the vector is [state, anim, anim_frame, hp, hitbox_active, poise, stamina, yaw, dist]).

P3 CONSUMPTION IN THE BROWSER (RI-MTH07): same player, same 8-attack script, same seed, four different targets. mat_flesh -> {hit_flesh_light:4}, material 'flesh'. mat_chitin -> {hit_chitin_light:4}, material 'chitin'. mat_stone -> {hit_chitin_light:3}, material 'stone'. mat_metal -> {hit_chitin_light:4}, material 'metal'. Same target moved from z=1.4 to z=6.0 -> {whiff:4} and no material at all. The voice the fight asks for moves when the world moves.

HONEST LIMIT on the above: RI-AUD01 §A defines exactly twelve classes and has NO stone or metal class, so mat_stone and mat_metal both route to C02 hit_chitin_light (the 'hard surface' class) while correctly carrying material 'stone'/'metal' on the event. The material reaches the audio layer; §A gives it only two buckets to land in. A wave-2 §A extension is where more would belong, not here.

MASS ROOT CAUSE IN CODE, CONFIRMED BY READING THE SOLVER'S OBJECTIVE: game/src/combat/swing.js:497 `calibrateYawGain` solves the per-clip yaw gain so that `measureActiveArc` equals the DECLARED arc, and `measureActiveArc` (same file) loops `for (f = startup+1; f <= startup+active; f++)` -- THE ACTIVE WINDOW ONLY. Its objective contains no tip-speed term, no frame-to-frame continuity term and no recovery term. So for any (declared arc, active_f, blade length) the solver will crank the gain to whatever angular velocity is needed and report success. That is why 43.4% of 606 clips exceed the §E tip-speed ceiling while `arc conformance` sits at 3.96%: the one thing that IS solved is the one thing that passes.

MASS: THE WHIP IS UNREACHABLE BY ANY GAIN, so this is a declaration problem and not a solver-tuning problem. whp_hist_bindings/r2 declares 305 deg over 11 active f@60 on a 3.114 m hilt-to-tip span, in the `medium` tier whose §E ceiling is 26 m/s. Holding 26 m/s at r=3.114 needs omega <= 8.35 rad/s = 7.97 deg/frame, i.e. >= 38 active frames for 305 deg. No value of yawGain reaches that; the arc, the active window or the tier has to move. HANDOVER: this is a change to weapon declarations touching up to 1,150 clips' bytes and other pieces hold determinism baselines against those bytes -- it should not land unreviewed. NOT FIXED BY ME, deliberately.

MASS: the follow-through failure is visible in the synthesised keys, not only in the tip path. `clip_w_whp_hist_bindings_r2` spine_00.ry keys are [[0,-22.581],[0.5,-53.878],[1,-38.549],[2,38.549],[2.26,38.549],[3,38.549]] -- phases 2 (last active), 2.26 (follow-through) and 3 (settle) all hold THE SAME VALUE, so the blade stops dead on the last active frame and holds for all 81 recovery frames. The same key list for clip_w_ssw_garrison_sword_r1_1 reads [[2,-12.293],[2.26 -> 2.24,-18.464],[3,-14.453]] -- overshoot then settle back, the correct §E shape. Both clips carry a healthy follow_frac in clip-registry.json (0.407 and 0.251), and only 6 of 1,150 clips have follow_frac <= 0 (all BOW), so the profile DATA is fine and the collapse happens downstream in synthesis.
